llm.summary: The skill's requirements line up with its stated purpose (managing a GitHub-backed skill repo), but its instructions give it write access to your repo and workspace and allow it to automatically pull and commit files from an external upstream — a supply-chain and privilege risk you should review before enabling.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to manage skills stored in a GitHub repo; requiring git, a GitHub PAT, and a config path (~/.anyskill/config.json) is consistent with cloning, reading index.json, and pushing commits as described.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent to auto-discover and read global/project config (including tokens), clone the repo, fetch index files, write/overwrite repository files (infra files) downloaded from an upstream GitHub repo, and update local workspace files (e.g., TOOLS.md). Those actions modify user files and can introduce code into your private repo; they go beyond passive read/search behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files — nothing is written to disk by an installer. That lowers immediate install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requesting a GitHub PAT and git is proportionate to the claimed functionality. The skill explicitly asks for a fine-grained PAT scoped to a single repo with Contents: Read and write; read-only would be sufficient if you only want to load/search. The SKILL.md also reads token from config, so the config file will contain sensitive material if used.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill will modify repository contents (committing downloaded infra files) and may write/update workspace config files (TOOLS.md). While always:false (not force-installed), it still has the ability to change system/project files and commit those changes to your repo — a significant privilege and potential supply-chain vector.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its purpose but has notable risks: it requires a GitHub PAT with repo write rights and will read/write ~/.anyskill/config.json and your specified localPath, clone and push to your private repo, and automatically download/overwrite infra files from the author's upstream repo. Before installing: 1) Only supply a fine-grained PAT scoped to the single repo you control; prefer read-only if you don't need upload/sync. 2) Inspect ~/.anyskill/config.json (or the project .anyskill.json) to ensure no unintended token storage. 3) Review exactly which upstream files it will fetch (the SKILL.md points at lanyijianke/AnySkill main) and decide whether you trust that upstream. 4) Disable any automatic apply/commit prompts or require explicit user confirmation for updates. 5) Consider using a disposable PAT and audits (review commits) if you permit write access. If you are uncomfortable with automatic writes to your repo or workspace files, do not enable this skill or restrict it to read-only usage.
